heading: INT. OCEAN LINER - REFRIGERATED HOLD - NIGHT

units.text: INT. OCEAN LINER - REFRIGERATED HOLD - NIGHT
Frost on iron.
Hanging sides of beef sway in the dim lamplight like pendulums.
The ship groans and creaks as it rolls.
Steam curls from every breath.
PROFESSOR EZEKIEL WARD (60s, heavy overcoat, goatee trimmed to a point, a leather medical bag) creeps between the carcasses, a lantern held high.
Behind him comes NURSE ANNELIESE KROLL (30s, white cap beneath a fur collar, face scrubbed pale), clutching a tin of ether.
Careful. The deck's slick.
units.name: WARD

units.text: It is the cold that frightens me, Professor, not the deck.
units.name: KROLL

units.text: Cold is the only honest thing aboard this vessel.
units.name: WARD

units.text: He swings the lantern.
The beam passes a crate stamped "PERISHABLE - HANDLE WITH CARE" and a second crate beside it, longer, narrower, its lid nailed down.
That is the one.
units.name: KROLL

units.text: So it is.
units.name: WARD

units.text: He kneels and prods the lid with a crowbar.
The nails shriek.
Kroll looks over her shoulder, then back, then over her shoulder again.
The ship lurches.

A beef side swings into her, and she gasps, shoves it away; Ward braces on the crate, wrenches the lid, and the two of them jerk backward as it clatters to the deck and a plume of frozen air sighs out of the dark, carrying a smell of salt and old flowers.
Dear God.
units.name: WARD

units.text: Inside lies a woman in a wedding dress of antique lace, her skin glittering with frost, her hands folded on her breast, eyes closed.
Roses, black with age, lie in her hair.
She is... she has not decayed.
units.name: KROLL

units.text: She cannot have been dead more than a day.
units.name: WARD

units.text: The ledger says fifty years.
units.name: KROLL

units.text: Ward leans in, lantern trembling.
The frost on her lashes begins to melt, beads sliding down her temple.
Kroll takes his arm.
Professor. Her eyes.
units.name: KROLL

units.text: The eyelids flutter.
Ward drops the lantern.
It shatters; the flame gutters.
In the dark, a thin whisper rises from the crate, one syllable, a word like "cold."
Kroll screams.

Ward throws his coat over the crate, and together they heave the lid back down, hammering it with the crowbar's flat end, and then stand panting in the sudden quiet, the swaying carcasses bumping them like drunken guests.
We did not hear that.
units.name: WARD

units.text: No, Professor.
units.name: KROLL

units.text: Behind them, from within the sealed crate, three polite knocks.
